audience: Curious general nonfiction readers who like Freakonomics-style questions, everyday economics, surprising data stories and practical ways to understand abstract systems without technical math.
author: Anton BV
citation_policy: Non-obvious factual or historical claims should trace to explicit sources; external index descriptions should retain source provenance.
description: Final pre-manuscript BookSpec candidate. The book is a compact, story-led popular nonfiction title about the ordinary objects and strange indicators people use to understand large economic and social systems, including why some measures illuminate and others become attractive nonsense.

execution_cost.notes: Use cheap structured API/provider tasks for bounded enrichment and research extraction; use human/Codex only for editorial judgment and manuscript quality gates.

expected_outcome: Human reviews Manuscript V1 and decides whether to proceed to BOOK-FACTORY-INDICES-005 Editorial QA + Fact Check Closure + Visual Plan.
illustration_policy: No custom illustration generation yet. Prefer text-first edition with charts/screenshots only after explicit rights review.

outline.notes: Open with Big Mac as familiar hook, then show why a purchasable object can make currency and cost-of-living abstraction readable.
outline.title: The Measure You Can Eat

outline.notes: Move from sticker prices to working hours, wages and lived affordability.
outline.title: Prices Become Human

outline.notes: Lipstick, men's underwear, hemlines and skyscrapers as memorable but contested economic folklore.
outline.title: The Folklore of Recession

outline.notes: Freight, shipping, containers and electricity show the physical economy underneath consumer life.
outline.title: The Economy Under the Economy

outline.notes: Cigarette-equivalent pollution and climate equivalence stories show the power and danger of translating risk into familiar units.
outline.title: Air You Can Count

outline.notes: Goodhart, manipulation, governance failures and stale indicators show how measures change behavior.
outline.title: When Measures Fight Back

outline.notes: AI benchmarks and readiness rankings as the newest family of seductive, contested indices.
outline.title: Benchmarks for Machines

outline.notes: Close with the practical reader payoff: how to distinguish useful proxies from myths, memes and manipulated targets.
outline.title: How to Read a Weird Index

positioning: Amazon-first popular economics and data-storytelling nonfiction. The title hook is object-led, but the manuscript promise is broader: ordinary objects and strange indicators can reveal, distort or manipulate how people understand the economy.
source_policy: Owner-originated material and approved ABVX content may be transformed. Third-party examples remain reference-only unless separately cleared.
subtitle: What Strange Indicators Really Tell Us About the Economy
title: Burgers, Lipstick & Underwear

translation.proper_name_policy: Not applicable for the seed edition because source and target language are the same.
